beats.intro_line: Hi, I'm Varun, and this video is about the honest machine — the rebuild that made the result hold up.

beats.narration_text: We rebuilt the system to be honest. Strict splits, an honesty band on every number, and a hard problem left deliberately open.

props.text:
We rebuilt the system to be faster.
Strict splits. Honest bands.

beats.series_slot: BODY ¶1 — THE TAUGHT CONCEPT: confidence intervals
beats.narration_text: First, we made the evaluation bulletproof. We split the patients cleanly — training and held-out testing kept strictly apart, by patient — and we stopped reporting a single lucky number. Instead we report a confidence interval: a range that says how much the result would wobble if we ran it again. Our clean O-C-T-only classifier lands around nought point eight six A-U-R-O-C, with that honesty band attached. A number you can actually trust.

props.sparkLine: A range, not a lucky number.
props.metricSub: OCT-only · patient-level split · with a confidence interval
props.caption: First-tier classifier, clean rebuild. The only performance figure in this episode.

beats.series_slot: BODY ¶2 — the fusion test that found nothing
beats.narration_text: Then we tested the tempting shortcut everyone reaches for: fusing the image with hand-computed structural measurements. We found they added almost nothing — the network had already learned that information from the image itself. A quietly important result: knowing what doesn't help is real progress too.

props.sparkLine: Knowing what does not help is progress.
props.caption: Conceptual. The fusion test added almost nothing.

beats.narration_text: And now, the frontier. We're testing whether today's most capable reasoning models — given only the honest, structural signal — can deliberate over the hard cases the way a specialist does, and explain every call. That experiment is live. We don't have the final answer yet. That's what ongoing research actually looks like — not a triumphant reveal, but a careful, honest climb.

roles: structural signal only — no visual field
frontier reasoning models over the hard cases
every call must come with an explanation
props.caption: Ongoing research. No result is claimed.

beats.series_slot: BODY ¶4 — the vision it builds toward
beats.narration_text: Here's the vision it's all building toward. A patient gets a quick, cheap O-C-T scan — anywhere. A fast model clears the easy cases and flags the uncertain ones. Those go to a reasoning model that lays out the evidence, and then to a human specialist with the case already worked up. The machine isn't the doctor. It's the tireless first reader that never gets bored, never skips a scan, and knows the edge of its own knowledge — buying back the one thing glaucoma steals: time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: which medical decisions should a machine be allowed to make, and which must always stay human? That line is ours to draw. Ask it to place three specific decisions on that line and defend each placement — and to say what evidence would move one across. If it won't commit, push back.

props.command: Which medical decisions should a machine be allowed to make — and which must always stay human? Place three specific decisions on that line, defend each placement, and tell me what evidence would move one across it.

beats.narration_text: From a pale-grey shimmer named by the Greeks, to a mirror in eighteen fifty, to a machine that reasons and admits doubt — the hunt has never moved faster. And the silent thief is running out of shadows. This has been The Uncertain Eye. The research continues — and so does the hunt.
